verdict.rationale: Microsoft's own Windows docs list an "Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10", which is a first-party mechanism for extended security update coverage. The evidence is only a single title-level mention, so it is unproven whether and how a power-user can enable it on their own installation. missing for 10: enrollment/enablement steps for individual users, the number of years of coverage, eligibility and cost details, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can enable extended years of security update coverage on my installation

citations.quote: Extended Security Updates (ESU) program for Windows 10
